title: Multi-stage builds
description: Learn how multi-stage Docker builds separate build-time tools from run-time images, producing smaller and more secure containers.

data.text: Production containers should contain only what they need to run. They should not carry compilers, SDKs, build tools, or test frameworks. Multi-stage builds make this practical by letting you use one full image to compile code and a separate minimal image to ship it.

A multi-stage build is a Dockerfile that contains more than one `FROM` instruction. Each `FROM` starts a new stage. You can copy artifacts from earlier stages into later stages, and only the final stage determines the image you ship. Earlier stages disappear from the final image, along with their tools, caches, and temporary files.

data.title: Why this matters
data.text: A single-stage build that compiles a .NET app with the SDK image ships the entire SDK. A multi-stage build copies only the compiled binary into a slim runtime image, cutting image size by 90 percent or more.

data.title: Go multi-stage build
data.content: The first stage uses the full Go SDK to compile the binary. The second stage uses a minimal scratch image. Only the compiled binary is copied forward.
data.code:
# Stage 1: build
FROM golang:1.23-alpine AS builder
WORKDIR /src
COPY go.mod go.sum ./
RUN go mod download
COPY . .
RUN CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -o /app/server .

# Stage 2: run
FROM scratch
COPY --from=builder /app/server /server
EXPOSE 8080
ENTRYPOINT ["/server"]

data.title: .NET multi-stage build
data.content: The SDK stage compiles the application. The ASP.NET runtime stage serves it. Only the compiled output and runtime dependencies are copied forward.
data.code:
# Stage 1: build
FROM mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/sdk:8.0 AS build
WORKDIR /src
COPY ["MyApp.csproj", "./"]
RUN dotnet restore
COPY . .
RUN dotnet publish -c Release -o /app/publish

# Stage 2: runtime
FROM mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/aspnet:8.0-alpine AS runtime
WORKDIR /app
COPY --from=build /app/publish ./
EXPOSE 8080
ENTRYPOINT ["dotnet", "MyApp.dll"]

data.title: Node.js multi-stage build
data.content: The first stage installs dependencies and builds the app. The second stage copies only the production node_modules and compiled assets.
data.code:
# Stage 1: build
FROM node:20-slim AS build
WORKDIR /app
COPY package.json package-lock.json ./
RUN npm ci
COPY . .
RUN npm run build

# Stage 2: runtime
FROM node:20-alpine AS runtime
WORKDIR /app
COPY --from=build /app/node_modules ./node_modules
COPY --from=build /app/dist ./dist
COPY package.json ./
EXPOSE 3000
CMD ["node", "dist/server.js"]

data.text: Every `FROM` instruction can be given a name with `AS <name>`. Named stages are easier to read and allow you to reference stages out of order. The final stage without a name, or with `AS runtime`, is the one that becomes the published image.

data.title: Stage naming conventions
items: Use descriptive names such as `builder`, `build`, `deps`, or `runtime`
Reference stages explicitly with `--from=builder` instead of relying on stage index
If you omit `AS name`, the stage is addressed by its numeric position starting from zero

data.text: The `COPY --from=<stage>` instruction is the bridge between stages. It copies files or directories from another stage's filesystem into the current stage. You can copy binaries, compiled assets, `node_modules`, configuration files, or anything else your runtime needs.

data.title: Copy only what you need
data.text: Do not copy the entire build stage. A full build stage contains source code, tests, and build tools. Copy only the artifacts the runtime actually uses. This keeps the final image minimal and reduces the attack surface.

BuildKit supports cache mounts with `RUN --mount=type=cache`. This lets you persist package manager caches between builds without committing them to an image layer. Combine cache mounts with multi-stage builds for the fastest and smallest images.

data.title: BuildKit cache mount for apt
data.content: The apt cache is persisted across builds but does not appear in any image layer.
data.code:
RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/var/cache/apt \
    --mount=type=cache,target=/var/lib/apt \
    apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends curl \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

data.title: Key takeaways
points: A multi-stage build uses multiple FROM instructions to separate build and runtime environments
Only the final stage becomes the published image, discarding build tools and intermediate files
Use COPY --from to move only the artifacts the runtime needs between stages
Named stages with AS make Dockerfiles easier to read and maintain
Combine multi-stage builds with BuildKit cache mounts for maximum build speed
data.takeaway: Multi-stage builds are the standard pattern for production Docker images: one stage to build, one stage to run.
